After the Second World War tens of thousands of Maltese emigrated, above all to Australia, under assisted passage schemes. Malta lost a large share of its young people in a few decades.

The islands were crowded and war-damaged, and work at the British dockyards was shrinking. The Maltese government and Australia paid for passages, and ships left Grand Harbour full of families. Others went to Canada, Britain and the United States.

Melbourne and Sydney gained large Maltese communities, with their own clubs, churches and festas. Many later returned home. The emigration eased unemployment in Malta before independence, and links with the diaspora remain strong. It was part of a wider wave of southern European migration, like that of Italians and Greeks.
